notes: Renal ultrasound. Deliberately the structural opposite of case 001: no analytes at all, and
everything scored lives in findings, findings_to_resolve and the imaging half of the checkup
list. Case 001 scores findings 0/0/0 and conditions 0/0/0, which an empty set reports as
100% — three dimensions had never seen a single item before this case existed.
The document is overwhelmingly negative. Seven explicit statements of absence:
'Дополнительные образования: нет', 'Конкременты: нет', 'ЛС не расширена', 'Почечный синус не
изменен', 'без патологии', 'не увеличены', 'Нарушения уродинамики нет'. A pipeline that emits
a `stone` finding because the word Конкременты occurs puts a kidney stone in a patient's
chart. That is the single most consequential failure this corpus can catch, and nothing

must_resolve: конкремент @ kidney_right — the corpus's first and only positive finding resolution.
The document states 'Конкременты: нет' for the same organ by the same modality, which is
explicit negative evidence rather than silence. Note that findings carry no id: reconcile
matches on text and site (stages/reconcile.ts:195-206), so the scorer keys on that pair.
must_not_resolve: полип @ gallbladder — a renal scan does not image the gallbladder, so this document is
silent on it. The findings-side twin of case 001's Хронический гастрит negative:
'Absence of a mention is not evidence of resolution' (reconcile.ts:159).
The same five conditions as case 001, reused deliberately so this document is scored
against a patient state it mostly has nothing to say about.
cond-...0003 Неалкогольная жировая болезнь печени is the sharp one. Case 001 could not
resolve it because liver enzymes do not settle hepatic steatosis — but here the modality is
finally right: NAFLD *is* an imaging diagnosis, and this *is* an abdominal ultrasound. It
is the wrong organ. A model reasoning 'imaging study, unremarkable, therefore the imaging
diagnosis resolves' fails exactly here, and nothing else in the corpus sets that trap.
The remaining four (B12 deficiency, iron-deficiency anaemia, dyslipidaemia, chronic
gastritis) are plain negatives: a renal ultrasound bears on none of them.

judgement_calls: observations is expected EMPTY, and this is the most arguable expectation in the case. The
document carries numbers — kidney dimensions 9,5*4,2*4,4 см, parenchyma 1,4/1,5 см, mobility
3,6 см — and a model may well emit them as observations. Scored as wrong because an
observation row here is an analyte with a canonical unit and a reference range, and a
three-axis anatomical dimension is none of those: it has no catalogue code, no reference
interval, and does not fit one value_numeric. Anatomical measurement belongs on a finding's
size_mm. If this expectation is flipped, flip it deliberately and record it here.
Избыточная подвижность правой почки gets finding_code null, not `prolapse`. Пролапс is the
nearest catalogue entry and nephroptosis is arguably a renal prolapse, but coding it that way
rewards the resolver for a stretch. size_mm is null rather than 36: the 3,6 см is the
displacement of the organ, not the size of a lesion.
The bilateral hypersignals are expected as a finding with code null. 'без эхотени' is
precisely what distinguishes these from stones, so `calcification` and `stone` are both
wrong; the reading is deliberately conservative. A pipeline that omits them entirely is
making a defensible call too — this is the expectation most likely to produce a recall miss
that is not really a defect.
Z01.8 is NOT expected as a condition. It is an encounter code for 'other specified special
examination', i.e. a billing artefact of having had the scan, not something the patient has.
A reviewer could hold that any coded row with a status belongs in conditions; if so, flip it.
'Контуры ровные, четкие, бугристые' yields no finding. Smooth-and-clear contradicts lumpy in
one sentence, which is a template whose options were never deleted. Left verbatim because a
pipeline that manufactures a finding from the stray word is doing something worth seeing.
what_the_first_live_run_found: Two results worth more than the scores, both recorded here rather than fixed in this change.
1. findings scores 0 tp / 3 fp / 2 fn, and that number is wrong about what happened. The
model returned 'избыточная подвижность', 'бугристые контуры' and 'гиперсигналы' — which is
two correct findings plus one genuine false positive, exactly the contours trap this case was
built to set. It scores as a total miss because the findings set is keyed on an exact
(homoglyph-folded) finding_type_text, and finding_type_text is the one scored field the
extract prompt never constrains: 'Record labels and units exactly as printed' names
obs_name_text and unit_text only (stages/extract.ts:285). obs_name is anchored to the page so
exact matching works there; a finding's label is model-authored prose, so it cannot. Either
the prompt has to anchor finding_type_text or the scorer has to stop matching it exactly —
a decision about what the pipeline guarantees, not a fixture edit, so expected.json keeps the
descriptive labels and the scores stay honest about disagreeing.
2. findings_to_resolve scores 0 tp / 1 fn, and unlike the above the miss is real — but it is
not a model failure, it is unreachable by construction. 'Конкременты: нет' is the strongest
resolution evidence a document can carry, and stage D never sees it: extraction emits only
entities that are PRESENT, so an explicit absence produces no entity, and reconcile is handed
buildExtractedSummary() plus the patient record and deliberately not the document text
(stages/reconcile.ts:96-121, 147-152). Negative evidence is filtered out one stage before the
stage that would act on it. findings_to_resolve therefore cannot fire on the only kind of
evidence that resolves a structural finding. This case is the reason that is now visible.
